sources.entry: Cockpit - Simple content platform to manage any structured content. (Source Code) MIT PHP

summary.one_liner: Cockpit is a headless, PHP-based content management system for managing structured content (collections, singletons, trees) exposed through REST and GraphQL APIs.
summary.what_it_does: Cockpit lets you define content models (collections, singletons, and trees) with custom fields, then edit that content in an admin UI. Content is served through REST and GraphQL APIs so any frontend, such as React, Vue, or mobile apps, can consume it. The README describes built-in multi-language support with fallback, user management with roles, permissions, 2FA and API tokens, and asset handling including image processing and video thumbnails. It also mentions a GraphQL playground, REST docs, CLI commands, custom fields, addons, hooks and events, and "spaces" for multiple sites. Storage can be SQLite (default) or MongoDB.
use_cases: Headless content backend for a website or JAMstack site
Content for IoT dashboards or displays
how_to_run: Option 1: download and extract the cockpit.zip archive, then cd into the cockpit directory
Make the storage directory writable (chmod -R 755 storage/)
Open the site in a browser and complete the setup
Option 2 (Docker): docker run -d --name cockpit -p 8080:80 -v cockpit_storage:/var/www/html/storage cockpithq/cockpit:core-latest
For MongoDB, use docker-compose with COCKPIT_DATABASE_SERVER and COCKPIT_DATABASE_NAME environment variables and mount a config/config.php file
Access the admin at the URL shown in the README (port 8080 in the Docker example)
notable: Headless design: works with any frontend framework via REST and GraphQL
Choice of SQLite for simple setups or MongoDB for production
Collections, singletons and trees with 20+ field types
Docker images published with core and pro tag lines
caveats: Requires PHP 8.3 or newer with PDO and GD extensions
Pro edition exists as separate pro-* Docker tags; README does not detail what pro adds
README links for download and admin URLs are missing in the extracted text, so exact URLs are unclear
